THE TUMOR CELLS STAIN FOR PROGESTERONE RECEPTOR PROTEIN. SEE NOTE. Note: In this laboratory, we used this antibody to stain 100 breast carcinomas prepared in the usual way (paraffin sections) and we compared the results with determinations of estrogen receptor by biochemical assay. 91% of tumors that stained with this antibody were positive for estrogen receptors by biochemical assay. 96% of tumors that failed to stain with this antibody were negative for estrogen receptors by biochemical assay. When we compared the results of staining of paraffin sections with the results of staining of frozen sections, the predictive value of a positive result was 97% and the predictive value of a negative result was 95%. In this laboratory, we also compared the results of staining of 100 routinely processed breast carcinomas with determinations of progesterone receptors by a hormone binding assay. Sixty-five percent of tumors that stained with this antibody contained progesterone receptors by the biochemical assay, and 98% of tumors that failed to stain lacked the receptors. THE RESULTS OF IMMUNOHISTOCHEMICAL STAINING FOR PROGESTERONE RECEPTOR PROTEIN ARE FOR INVESTIGATIONAL USE ONLY. THEY MUST NOT BE USED FOR CLINICAL PURPOSES. PATHOLOGIC DIAGNOSIS: 
CONSULT SLIDES FROM SOUTH SHORE HOSPITAL, SOUTH WEYMOUTH, MA: 
LEFT SENTINEL LYMPH NODES ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ; 1/20/06): 
Two (2) sentinel lymph nodes negative for carcinoma, see note. 
Note: By report, two atypical cells were seen on the touch preps during 
intraoperative consultation. No atypical cells were seen on any of the HE 
histologic sections or keratin ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) stains. 
LEFT BREAST, WIRE LOCALIZED EXCISION FOR A MASS AND A CLIP WITH ADDITIONAL 
MEDIAL MARGIN AND PORTACATH SCAR TISSUE ( REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ; 6/15/06): 
Residual INVASIVE DUCTAL CARCINOMA, poorly differentiated (modified 
Bloom-Richardson grade III/III), with calcifications present as two foci 0.4cm 
and 0.2cm (blocks  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID  and  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ), see note. 
No lymphovascular invasion present. 
No in situ carcinoma present. 
Invasive carcinoma is 0.1cm from the deep margin (inked black; block  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID ) and 
0.1cm from the superficial margin (inked blue; block  REMOVED_ACCESSION_ID , level 2RC). The 
superior, inferior, medial, and lateral margins are negative for carcinoma. 
The additional medial margin shows benign breast tissue and is negative for 
carcinoma. 
One intramammary lymph node negative for carcinoma. 
Calcifications in normal breast epithelium. 
The portacath scar tissue specimen shows fibroadipose tissue with foreign body 
giant cell response and chronic inflammation. 
Note: By report, this patient received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. The 
pre-treatment size of the tumor in the upper outer quadrant was REMOVED_DATE x REMOVED_DATE x REMOVED_DATE 
cm based on an outside MRI (1/9/06), and there was an area of enhancement (0.5 
cm) at 6:00 2cm inferior to the nipple (no mass at 6:00 on ultrasound). The 
post-treatment MRI (5/10/06) showed dramatic improvement with resolution of the 
mass and only a few foci of punctate enhancement seen around the clip site. 
The enhancing area at 6:00 was no longer present. Grossly, no mass was 
identified, but a specimen radiograph showed calcifications (no clip mentioned 
in the gross description). Microscopically, there were two foci (0.4cm and 
0.2cm ) of residual invasive carcinoma within a histologic tumor bed. The size 
of the histologic tumor bed is difficult to estimate, since no gross mass was 
seen; however, it measures approximately 1.7cm on the glass slide. The 
overall estimated cellularity is 5%. This corresponds to a Miller-Payne grade
